title: House Democrats Launch Probe Into Epstein's Alleged Role as Foreign Agent
excerpt: Rep. Jamie Raskin says documents reveal 'substantial evidence' the late sex offender advanced interests of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Russia, and Israel while never registering as a foreign agent.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Rep. Jamie Raskin is investigating Epstein's potential role as an unregistered foreign agent.
  • Epstein allegedly advanced interests of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Russia, and consulted for Israel.
  • Raskin is seeking records from the DOJ, State Department, and intelligence community.
  • Around 2.5 million Epstein-related documents remain unreleased by the DOJ.
  • Rep. Jamie Raskin has launched an investigation into whether Jeffrey Epstein acted as an unregistered foreign agent for multiple countries.
  • Documents reveal Epstein allegedly advanced interests of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Russia, and consulted for a former Israeli prime minister.
  • Raskin is requesting records from the DOJ, State Department, and intelligence community on Epstein's foreign contacts.
  • Approximately 2.5 million Epstein-related documents remain unreleased by the Department of Justice.

The Investigation

Rep. Jamie Raskin, the top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee, has launched a formal investigation into whether Jeffrey Epstein operated as an unregistered foreign agent for multiple governments, requesting records from the Trump administration on the scope of the late convicted sex offender's foreign ties.

https://x.com/factpostnews/status/2079589789326606400

In a letter sent Monday, Raskin pointed to documents released by the Department of Justice and the House Oversight Committee, stating he has found "substantial evidence" that Epstein "acted to advance the interests" of Saudi Arabia and Kuwait, advised the Russian government, and worked as a consultant for a former Israeli prime minister.

> **"Epstein's activities on behalf of foreign states."

— Rep."**

"Epstein's activities on behalf of foreign states." — Rep."

"Our examination of available evidence has already revealed damning indications of Mr. Epstein's activities on behalf of foreign states."

— Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member, House Judiciary Committee

What the Evidence Shows

Raskin's letter details what he describes as Epstein's multi-country lobbying operation. According to the congressman, documents show Epstein engaged in activities on behalf of at least four foreign governments — Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Russia, and Israel — without ever registering under the Foreign Agents Registration Act, which requires individuals acting on behalf of foreign powers to disclose their activities to the Department of Justice.

The investigation also raises security concerns. Raskin highlighted potential risks posed by Epstein's foreign ties, given his extensive access to powerful figures in American politics, business, and academia. Epstein, who died by suicide in a Manhattan jail cell in August 2019 while awaiting trial on federal sex trafficking charges, maintained relationships with numerous high-profile individuals across multiple administrations.

Political Dynamics and Unresolved Questions

In the Republican-controlled House, Raskin's demands to the Department of Justice, Department of State, and intelligence community are unlikely to receive immediate compliance. However, the investigation serves as a preview of how Democrats plan to pursue the Epstein case if they reclaim the House majority, which would give them subpoena power over committees.

Raskin believes critical evidence may be buried within approximately 2.5 million Epstein-related documents that the Department of Justice has not yet released. He is requesting any records related to Epstein's interactions with foreign officials and calling on the DOJ to provide a written response addressing whether there has ever been an investigation into Epstein's potential role as a foreign agent.

The probe adds to an expanding Democratic investigation into Epstein's networks. In recent weeks, Raskin has also demanded records from Bard College and Harvard University over their ties to Epstein, alleging that the sex offender used his connections to elite academic institutions to facilitate trafficking operations.

The Scope of the Investigation
›Raskin requests records from DOJ, State Department, and intelligence agencies.
›Approximately 2.5 million documents related to Epstein remain unreleased.
›Investigation highlights potential security risks from Epstein's foreign ties.
›Democrats may pursue further investigations if they regain House majority.

What Comes Next

The investigation marks a significant escalation in congressional scrutiny of Epstein's foreign connections — an area that has received comparatively less attention than his domestic crimes. While the Republican majority is unlikely to advance the probe in the current Congress, the requests establish a documentary record and public pressure campaign that could intensify ahead of the 2028 elections.

CNN, the DOJ, the State Department, and the Office of the Director of National Intelligence have been contacted for comment on Raskin's requests. The investigation also comes amid a separate dispute between New Mexico's attorney general and the federal government over access to evidence from Epstein's Zorro Ranch property, where the first documented law enforcement search occurred in March 2020, according to the Associated Press.
